title: Palmitoylethanolamide ameliorates neuroinflammation via modulating PPAR-alpha to promote the functional outcome after intracerebral hemorrhage.
authors: Zhou, Guoyang; Fu, Xiongjie; Wang, Liang; Cao, Yang; Zhuang, JianFeng; Hu, Junwen; Li, Yin; Xu, Chaoran; Gao, Shiqi; Shao, Anwen; Wang, Lin
one_liner_zh: 该文研究棕榈酰乙醇酰胺通过PPAR-alpha调节脑出血后神经炎症，属于神经药理学湿实验，无蛋白质-DNA互作、无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Intracerebral hemorrhage is a type of acute cerebrovascular disease that remains one of the main causes of death and disability. After the onset of ICH, different types of severe pathophysiological changes can cause great damage to brain tissue, including neuroinflammation. Our study demonstrated the effect of PEA on modulating microglia phenotype and neuroinflammation, as well as the possible underlying mechanisms after ICH for the first time. The phenotypic transformation of microglia and simulation of neuroinflammation after ICH in vitro was induced by hemoglobin on BV2 cells. Additionally, the experiment in vivo model was induced by collagenase injection in mice. The role of PEA on hematoma clearance was also discussed. Western blot, ELISA and immunofluorescence staining were used to determine the phenotypic polarization of microglia and neuroinflammation. In order to evaluate the role of PPAR-alpha in the anti-inflammatory effect of PEA after ICH, the PPAR-alpha antagonist GW6471 was utilized. Behavior tests examined the effect of PEA on improving neuronal function. Our results showed that PEA can ameliorate neuroinflammation by inhibiting upregulation of NF-kappaB, IL-1beta and TNF-alpha, both in vivo and in vitro. Additionally, PEA can improve motor function in ICH mice and promotes hematoma clearance. At the same time, PEA can increase the levels of PPAR-alpha in the nucleus. Hence, PPAR-alpha antagonists can reverse the protective effects of PEA on neuroinflammation. These results suggest that PEA is involved in microglia polarization, attenuating the activation of neuroinflammation, as well as improving motor function after ICH. This, at least in part, may contribute to the involvement of PPAR-alpha modulation of NF-kappaB.
abstract_zh: 脑出血是一种急性脑血管疾病，仍是导致死亡和残疾的主要原因之一。脑出血发病后，不同类型的严重病理生理变化可对脑组织造成巨大损害，包括神经炎症。我们的研究首次证明了PEA在调节小胶质细胞表型和神经炎症中的作用，以及脑出血后可能的潜在机制。在体外，通过血红蛋白诱导BV2细胞模拟脑出血后小胶质细胞的表型转化和神经炎症。此外，在体内实验中，通过向小鼠注射胶原酶建立模型。还探讨了PEA对血肿清除的作用。采用Western blot、ELISA和免疫荧光染色确定小胶质细胞的表型极化和神经炎症。为了评估PPAR-α在PEA抗炎作用中的作用，使用了PPAR-α拮抗剂GW6471。行为学测试检查了PEA对改善神经元功能的影响。我们的结果表明，PEA在体内和体外均可通过抑制NF-kappaB、IL-1beta和TNF-alpha的上调来改善神经炎症。此外，PEA能改善脑出血小鼠的运动功能并促进血肿清除。同时，PEA能增加细胞核中PPAR-α的水平。因此，PPAR-α拮抗剂可以逆转PEA对神经炎症的保护作用。这些结果表明，PEA参与小胶质细胞极化，减轻神经炎症的激活，并改善脑出血后的运动功能。这至少部分可能归因于PPAR-α对NF-kappaB的调节作用。
